$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `files`' canonical store, the
THIRTEENTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 s15 gives the
ORM. One entry per guard: per scope predicate, per range check that stands
where no CHECK stands, per clause of a statement the port's contract depends
on, and per read decision that keeps a row an older binary wrote readable.
Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it
(`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen
to go red (`kills`).
IT IS AN ELEVENTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json, mutations-cost.json, mutations-channels.json,
mutations-governance.json, mutations-secrets.json, mutations-providers.json,
mutations-conversations.json, mutations-skills.json and
mutations-memory.json rather than an extension of any of them, for the
reason the fourth was: each tranche is a separate claim about a separate
port surface, and a reader checking one should not have to read past the
others. All are hashed by the same packages.adapters.config rule and counted
together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. THIS CONTEXT'S TWO TABLES ARE
UNUSUALLY WELL CONSTRAINED and the interesting guards are therefore NOT the
usual vocabulary checks. There is a real CHECK behind `Artifact.metadata`
and a real rule behind every ancestry, so `files-rows.ts` re-validates only
what the database leaves open — and what it leaves open is exactly the
arithmetic. `bytes`, `width`, `height`, `durationSec` and `revision` carry
NO CHECK at all: a negative byte count is headroom a tenant did not buy, and
a zero revision makes `latest + 1` collide with the first revision the
append-only unique already holds.
AND THE SCOPE IS NOT ON THE ROW. Both tables store `environmentId` and
nothing above it, while both aggregates carry a full `EnvironmentScope` —
three ids. So every scoped read carries FOUR clauses over three joined
tables and every write re-asserts an ancestry no database rule checks, and
the sweep's job is to prove that each of those clauses is doing work rather
than standing next to one that is.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite SET unmutated and refuses to
sweep unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies
a run with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE INTEGRATION SUITES RUN ON A REAL POSTGRESQL, in a container, on the
machine that has a daemon. `files-rows.test.ts` is the only suite here that
runs without one, and it is the one that reaches the two unreadable-row
branches a container cannot: an unresolved ancestry, which the schema's own
foreign keys make unreachable from a live database, and a summed byte total
past 2^53, which would need nine petabytes of attachments in one
EVERY `from` IS A UNIQUE SUBSTRING OF ITS FILE and is applied literally, so
a sweep that silently matched nothing is impossible: the driver refuses an
entry whose `from` occurs zero times or more than once, and records it as
EVERY `kills` ENTRY IS THE FULL NAME OF A CASE THE DRIVER WATCHED GO RED,
parsed out of the run rather than written down beforehand.

sweep: MEASURED on a real PostgreSQL (pgvector/pgvector:pg16) in a container, on
the machine that has a daemon. THIRD AND FINAL RUN: 80 entries, 80 KILLED,
0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS, 0 UNAPPLIED.
THE BASELINE IS PROVED FIRST AND THE DRIVER REFUSES TO SCORE WITHOUT IT.
Each distinct suite set was run UNMUTATED and had to exit zero with a
non-zero executed case count before any mutation was applied.
THE FIRST SWEEP IS PART OF THE RESULT AND IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN
DISCARDED: 80 entries, 73 KILLED, 7 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS. SIX of the seven
survivors were cases passing for the wrong reason, and they had ONE cause.
EVERY CROSS-TENANT CASE NAMED THE FOREIGN CHAIN, WHICH DIFFERS IN ALL THREE
IDS AT ONCE. That is what a real caller looks like, and it is exactly why it
could not tell which clause did the work: a read that had dropped its
ENVIRONMENT clause still answered `null` for a request whose project and
organization were also foreign. M-F30 and M-F36 are that failure on the
attachment read and on the dedupe probe, and the harness now seeds a SECOND
environment of the SAME project so the clause can be isolated.
M-F53, M-F54 AND M-F58 ARE THE SAME SHAPE ONE TABLE OVER. Every artifact
read was asked of a key that was the only one in its thread and a thread that
was the only one in its environment, so the key clause and the thread clause
were both answered by their neighbours. Two keys in one thread and two
threads in one environment are the shapes that separate them.
M-F65 IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE MATTERED MOST. The erasure COUNT and the
erasure LISTING are two statements carrying the same subject clause, and only
the listing was asserted — so the count could have lost its filter while every
case passed, and an erasure PLAN would have promised destruction of rows
belonging to somebody else. The count is now required to equal the listing's
length.
AND THE SEVENTH SURVIVOR WAS NOT A MISSING CASE. M-F41 removes
`COALESCE(SUM(...), 0)`, and the clause turned out to be unfalsifiable: a SQL
NULL reaching `readTotalBytes` was compared with
`null > 9007199254740991n`, which JavaScript coerces to false, and
`Number(null)` is 0 — the right answer by accident. `readTotalBytes` now
checks the TYPE, which makes the clause falsifiable and closes the accident
at the same time: a SQL NULL where the port promises a number is a defect,
not a zero.
THE SECOND SWEEP, after those five cases and that one guard, killed all
eighty. The third run is the same result with the killing case NAMES
captured, which is what this file records.
